#3897. 13 arrested in Shanghai as police crackdown on bootleg Final Fantasy 7 Tifa figurine operation

Chinese police have arrested 13 individuals in Shanghai allegedly involved in a bootleg Final Fantasy 7 Tifa figurine business, after consumers reported the operation. They are currently being investigated on suspicion of selling infringing reproductions.

Reported by Gamespark, the police cracked down on the operation which involved the seizure of around $300,000 of goods related to the figurines.

The investigation started in May, after police received reports from concerned members of the public about the Tifa figurines. They were made from different materials than official figurines, and after confirming the illegitimacy of these products with the rights holders, Square Enix, police determined these businesses were not authorised to be producing such goods and went to work.

The appearance of these counterfeits were deemed identical to the real merch, and therefore the alleged crime was deemed infringement of official goods. These counterfeits also came in different sizes, some of which were more expensive than the originals and customisabile.

Looking at pictures taken by local outlet Shangguan News (and put side-by-side by Automaton), you can see the official Tifa figurine (right) next to the counterfeit version (left). Both show Tifa in a blue dress, though the materials used are clearly different.

#3896. The Sunday Papers

The Sunday Papers is our weekly roundup of great writing about (mostly) videogames from across the web.

Sundays are for googling local purveyors of live Christmas trees, the sole upside of no longer having a cat being that you can once again enjoy the smell of chopped woodland without the risk of it poisoning a family member. Turns out Fortnite players are more loyal.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Sony has been crowing about Grand Theft Auto 6 setting a new record for concurrent PlayStation players, which isn't bad for a game that's currently only singleplayer. It isn't just beating the records set by the giants of multiplayer gaming back when they released, though. It's also eating their lunch right now.

Alinea Analytics reports that Call of Duty, Fortnite, and EA Sports FC 27 all saw their number of daily active users drop when GTA 6 released. "Call of Duty got it the worst of the three," Alinea's head of market analysis Rhys Elliott wrote, "dropping 42% from an average of 7.5M DAUs to 4.4M" according to the company's estimates.

Fortnite only lost 28% of its players, the firm claims based on PlayStation and Xbox data—Alinea's Fortnite figures do not take Switch, mobile, or Epic Games Store players into account—An estimated five million of them choosing to buy groceries and fix the stairs instead of parachuting out of a bus over the weekend. EA Sports FC 27 suffered a similar loss. "FC 27's DAUs dropped by about 27% when GTA 6 launched," according to Elliott, "from 5.9M to 4.3M."

But where player numbers for both of those games were trending back up four days after GTA 6's release, Call of Duty has struggled to win its players back, Elliott says: "Sadly, CoD has barely bounced back after four days. It's still down 41% from its baseline."

During that time Call of Duty had a Thanksgiving-themed event, while FC 27 had a Black Friday discount and in-game "Thunderstruck" promotion, and Fortnite's ongoing Treasure Hunters event is adding a bunch of One Piece stuff. If you're going up against a cultural juggernaut like GTA, I guess crossing over with something as massive as One Piece is the way to do it.

As Elliott concludes, this is only part one of the story. When Rockstar comes back for the second bite of this apple its rivals might have an even harder fight on their hands: "When the online component and PC port of GTA 6 hits (some time next year simultaneously, I'd imagine), then the bounce back will not be so obtainable."

#3893. Undisclosed AI-generated music pulled from The Binding of Isaac Repentance+ update, as attempt to get satirical on GTA 6 launch day goes awry

Original creator Edmund McMillen said he "had no idea [the update] featured generated music in the daily run"

An update for The Binding of Isaac packed with wink wink, nudge nudge parody of GTA 6 has backfired rather spectacularly, with publishers Nicalis having to make some hasty modifications. This free addition to the Repentance+ version of the roguelike featured a Grand Terry Auto-inspired daily run, complete with cops, guns, and a soundtrack players soon highlighted as sounding AI-generated. Sure enough, Nicalis subsequently announced the "removal of generated music files" in response to the backlash.

The Repentance+ update went live on November 19th to coincide with GTA 6's release, and the music files had been yanked by Nicalis as of November 21st. In the interim, a Reddit user with the handle ShweetsStuff unearthed metadata pointing to AI tune generator Suno attached to some of the update's music files. Cue understandable questioning of why the DLC's Steam page hadn't had a disclosure of this genAI use slapped across it.

Original Binding of Isaac creator Edmund McMillen seems to have quickly ended up with inboxes full of folks asking him about what'd happened and demanding action. "Woke up to a shit show," he posted on the former Twitterverse on the 21st. Obviously I had no idea it featured generated music in the daily run, looking into how that happened and getting it removed, stay tuned."

Given the new build yanking the music went live later that day, McMillen's voice maybe only added to the chorus of complaints Nicalis were already aware of and facing. Either way, the songs are gone and Nicalis don't look to have said anything as of writing about whether they'll be replaced at some point down the line.

This isn't the first time a developer has considered using AI to generate songs designed to satirise or parody. In the case of Future? No Thanks! dev Paolo 'Molleindustria' Pedercini, the aim was partly to poke fun at disclosures, with people in the game's future society listening to AI-generated tunes that're corporately mandated to mention AI in the lyrics. Pedercini ended up deciding not to use AI-generated music in the final release.

On the face of it, while the effectiveness of using AI-generated songs to parody AI-generated songs is questionable, the argument for it seems stronger in a more focused satire like Future? No Thanks! than in the case of The Binding of Isaac having a GTA 6-related giggle. I've not listened to the Repentance+ update's AI tunes, but there's nothing obvious to indicate that their satirical job wouldn't have been done as well or better by Nicalis commissioning or otherwise employing someone to pen some entirely human-made ditties, that spoofed the nature of Large Stealy Wheely.

Perhaps the publishers will now go and do just that.

#3892. Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang accused of decades of bullying and workplace abuse in new investigation

Public humiliation reportedly considered a "rite of passage".

An investigation into the workplace behavior of Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang, who resigned recently after a series of extramarital affairs came to light, has uncovered decades of harassment, verbal employee abuse and "cultish" behaviour at the company which has long played a major role in PC gaming.

Following Huang's departure, The New York Times has published a report in which "more than a dozen" current and former Nvidia employees discussed their experiences with the former CEO. Speaking on conditions of anonymity, employees alleged Jensen Huang would verbally berate them, reportedly going as far as to say he'd rip their arms off, rip their heart out and stomp on it, or rip their head off and "pee on your brain".

The report includes numerous examples of Huang's alleged abusive behaviour, which apparently stretches back years before Nvidia became the one of the most valuable companies in the world - years before the AI boom. It's claimed Huang on one occasion went around a room of managers telling them he'd kill them. Then, when he reached a person in their 70s, said everyone hoped they'd drop dead.

Huang allegedly referred to these bouts of public humiliation as a "rite of passage" at Nvidia, when questioned by an internal HR employee whom he later fired for not being a "right fit". Huan's stance was apparently to test whether a person could handle the culture there, which is described in the report as "cultish".

It's claimed Huang's influence at Nvidia has meant other senior managers have followed his lead, including his daughter Madison, Nvidia's chief of staff, who it's said often yells at staff, including executives more highly ranked than her.

A spokesperson for Huang denied the allegations in response to a request for comment by the New York Times. The spokesperson, John Fisher, said the claims in the report were "fabrications that are now impossible to disprove specifically, and the thousands of Nvidia employees who continue to speak out for Jensen show they’re false".

Huang resigned from his role as Nvidia CEO earlier this month after a series of extramarital affairs were unearthed - one with a person US intelligence believes to be a Chinese spy, and two others with Nvidia employees. The chair of Nvidia's board, Harvey C. Jones, reportedly said earlier this week that the company "does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO".

The answer is Grand Theft Auto 6, of course. Rockstar has once again created a masterclass open world game, arguably the greatest yet (thanks to its massive budget).

There is a singular word that defines their games: moments. Rockstar knows how to create interesting moments throughout the entire game to not only feel unique, but personal, as if it was put into place at a specific time just for you to encounter and maybe nobody else.

Interestingly, I love the game but I don’t spend much time playing. It’s such a dense game that I want to take my sweet time with it, and experience what each town and county has to offer. I don’t care if it will take months to beat the game—because the entire game is another Rockstar “moment”.

One of these moments occurred when I was dirt biking up in the hills. I heard commotion off the beaten path so I go explore the noises. There were two friends hunting. One guy is dressed up in a deer outfit, and his buddy “accidentally” shot him. They ask me to grab their truck and take them the hospital. On the way the two start arguing in the backseat, with the guy who got shot saying it was done on purpose because he slept with his wife. All hell broke loose, and they were fighting over the shotgun. The guy who originally got shot ended up blowing the head off his friend during the struggle, and pushed him out of the car. I finish the drive to the hospital and the man thanks me, giving me his shotgun as a thank you gift.

In another incident, I’m cruising the backroads with Lucia when she notices three people on a bridge. Two of the guys are tempting the other to jump off into the water. Lucia tells me to slow down and check it out. All of the guys are getting drunk and acting stupid, and they dare us two to jump. We agree, hold hands, and jump into the water. The other two guys start laughing saying, “Thanks for your ride, idiots!” and stole my car.

This game is so full of these random moments. GTA VI is simply a generational piece of fiction. To its characters, the writing, mechanics, exploration, and other details, it’s a new bench mark for gaming.

I love making stuff go boom in GTA 6. I've always loved the cover shooter antics of Rockstar's action-adventure series, but sometimes you need a nice big explosion to clear up the crowd. Since the vast GTA 6 map of Leonida is a veritable powder keg just waiting for me to pop a bullet into its many, many car engines, I thought it would be cool to try out some action hero stunts early on in the process.

One main GTA 6 mission saw me defending "work colleague" Donnie from waves of biker gang enemies, ducking behind cover and holding them off while my partner brought the plane around so we could make a grand escape. But indulging my desire for big explosions left me with one ill-fated choice: do a cardio workout or die trying.

In a departure from past entries, GTA 6 is all about due restraint. I bear this in mind as I pop shots into the gang members, aiming for kneecaps, torsos, and limbs over vitals. A few more bikers arrive, screeching to a halt in a nice little cluster. There's too many of them, and I'm quickly becoming overwhelmed. I enter Focus Mode to zero in on the engine tanks and do what I do best: fire off an entire clip into one of them. A cataclysmic boom clears the crowd in a satisfying blast of fire, smoke, and biker boy chunks.

Donnie, of course, chooses that exact moment to tell me to grab a bike and hop on the plane with him. The only problem is that there are no motorbikes before me, but a heap of smoldering chassis.

I panic and run up to one that looks more intact than the others. To my horror, the engine is completely dead. I race to another, and the tank is out of fuel. I turn and watch Donnie soar into the skies, telling me to meet him on the road, right as I hear another wave of enemies roar onto the scene. I don't think – I just run off toward the nearest body of water.

I have no plan. Maybe I can lose my pursuers in the bushes, I wonder, or maybe some kind NPC will have left me a speedboat or canoe or set of flotation devices – anything, anything to get me out onto the water and away from the bikers as fast as possible – but of course there is nothing but open water. I open the map to check Donnie's whereabouts. Wherever he is doesn't look that far off, so I leap into the water without a second thought

My frantic front-crawl is the last bastion of hope I cling to as bullets continue to fly overhead. Each one pierces the water's surface with delicate precision, yet further evidence of the game's painstaking realism. But as the bullets stop and the combat music fades, I realize with a jolt that I am doing it. I'm doing it! I'm swimming to safety!

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

Alas, I am in Leonida, not an Olympic swimming pool. One moment, there's nothing but murky greenish-brown water all around. Then, a gator emerges in that sneaky, silent way, one only a prehistoric beast that has evaded extinction across millions of years knows how to. So like a true Florida man, I stop in my tracks and pivot to punch the gator in the face.

I'm here to warn you, dear reader, that not even max-muscle Jason can fight a gator in the middle of a swamp. It grabs me in its terrifying jaws and spins, the deathly move that few creatures can escape – least of all a dude in flip flops and a wifebeater. Consider this a humble PSA for all my fellow explosion-fanatics. Making stuff go boom is a riot and a half, but being eaten by an alligator is not worth the spectacle.

#3889. GTA 6 credits actually include 'Florida Joker', the viral internet personality who once demanded $10 million from Rockstar Games

Lawrence Sullivan, better known to the online world as the 'Florida Joker', is in GTA 6. After accusing Rockstar Games of using his likeness without consent and then demanding a $10m payout, the two parties have seemingly settled their differences.

Grand Theft Auto 6's earliest controversy came from its very first official trailer, when Sullivan alleged one of the teaser's similarly tattooed characters was modeled after him. The former tattoo model, who first went viral because of a mugshot that shared an uncanny resemblance to Batman's Joker, soon called on Rockstar to pay him $2m. His demand quickly shot up to $10m, before he dropped all legal threats and politely asked to officially work with the developer.

Rockstar seems to have relented to that last request - the vast GTA 6 credits include none other than one Lawrence Sullivan, listed under the 'Local Population' cast, alongside dozens of other names.

GTA 6 players wasted no time, and quickly found the suspect first teased way back in that original 2023 trailer. In its quest to parody all parts of modern life under capitalism, GTA 6 lets you doomscroll through a social media app called Snapmatic, which flings an endless number of short-form clips and thirst traps at you. If you're lucky enough, or if you scroll for long enough, you'll find a video of Sullivan's in-game counterpart beating up a fake lookalike. He certainly sounds like Sullivan, too.

"Two years y'all been talking crazy about me," he wrote under a recent Instagram post. "Who got the last laugh now?!"

The GTA 6 credits were illuminating for other reasons, too. We finally know who voices the game's loveable duo, Jason and Lucia, for one. All 34 of the infamously fired Rockstar workers also appear in GTA 6's credits. The controversial move eventually led to accusations of union busting on Rockstar's part, which is currently being investigated as part of an employment tribunal in Scotland.

#3888. Nvidia release hotfix for latest graphics card driver battering SSDs with excessive writes, but it looks like reverting may still be the better option

621.35 appears not to completely atone for 621.24's sins

Late last week, reports emerged of some folks having Nvidia's latest GeForce driver, 621.24, needlessly write vast amounts of data to their PC's SSD, a bug that could affect the component's lifespan at a time when replacing SSDs certainly isn't cheap. The immediate short-term solution for affected users was to roll back to a previous driver, 621.01. Sadly it appears that might still be the best way to go despite Nvidia having released a hotfix.

The hotfix, driver version 621.35, was released on November 20th and as of writing is only available to download directly from the Nvidia website. It's designed to address one issue, this being that "excessive writes to file nvlog.nvlgstg may occur in background".

"Since we have so many changes being checked in, we usually try to align driver releases with significant game or product releases," Nvidia wrote in their announcement of the hotfix. "This process has served us pretty well over the years but it has one significant weakness. Sometimes a change that is important to many users might end up sitting and waiting until we are able to release the driver. The fixes that make it in are based in part on your feedback in the Driver Feedback threads and partly on how realistic it is for us to quickly address them. These fixes (and many more) will be incorporated into the next official driver release, at which time the hotfix driver will be taken down.

"To be sure, these Hotfix drivers are beta, optional and provided as-is. They are run through a much abbreviated QA process. The sole reason they exist is to get fixes out to you more quickly. The safest option is to wait for the next WHQL certified driver. But we know that many of you are willing to try these out."

Unfortunately, it seems that based on some testing by users on r/Nvidia, the hotfix makes the situation with excessive SSD writing less bad than it is with 621.24, but doesn't eliminate the problem entirely. According to one of these users, 621.35 stops the excessive writing from starting right after you boot up and reduces the amount that's being written when the issue's at its peak, but doesn't prevent some excessive writing creeping in if hardware is left running for extended periods or left idling overnight.

Given that, rolling back to 621.01 still appears to be the most effective way of keeping the writes at an acceptable level while waiting for Nvidia to release a new driver than can permanently do away with the problem. One would hope it won't take too long, especially given the 621.24 driver still doesn't look to have been pulled offline so no one else grabs it prior to a fix arriving.

If you want to check if you're suffering from the excessive writing you'll need to open task manager, head to the 'details' tab, right click on the column header, click 'select columns', select 'I/O write bytes' from the menu of check boxes that brings up, then look for 'NVDisplay.Container.exe'. The number next that exe is in bytes, so you'll need to do some maths to work out if it's only writing a matter of MB or chunks of GB.

Learning things about your partner by spending time with them? Say it ain't so.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

My real relationship be damned, this last week has been all about playing cupid in Grand Theft Auto 6. I've become utterly invested in keeping Jason and Lucia in love, which means a lot of my time in the game has been spent doing things with my partner in tow. Hitting the gym, inviting them out for a late-night bite, robbing a few jewellery stores. You know, couple things. Things couples do.

And, as people tend to do when they're spending a lot of time together, Jason and Lucia talk. A lot. And you know what? Some of the best nuggets of information about their lives—both their time spent together before the events of the game, and their own individual lives before meeting one another—are tucked away in these interactions that fill the game's quieter moments.

Sometimes the interactions are simply fluffy, or funny. Lucia poking fun at Jason for his deep voice and monosyllabic responses, or them reminiscing about little moments that happened in their relationship before the whole "Lucia ghosting Jason and ending up in jail" thing. Sometimes it's Lucia getting a spam call and giving the bot (and eventual human) on the other end of the phone an absolute earful.

But then, occasionally, beyond all the comedic conversations and flavour dialogue that give these characters so much life, the game'll drop some proper good lore. I'll do my best not to spoil stuff here, but for almost every complaint I've seen on social media about why certain protagonists did certain things, there's an answer tucked away in these interactions. The kind of things you'd really want to know about these characters? Your best chance of finding it all out is when you bring them together.

I've really enjoyed having lore drops unfold in mundane conversations while walking around, driving, or eating a burger, rather than hamfisted into the main story. They feel like natural breathing moments for the couple to recount the past, or get into the stuff that was happening in the time that they were apart. You know, the exact kind of times actual couples and friends would find the time to dig into these things in real life, too.

That doesn't mean you have to keep them together all the time. Some of their exclusive missions also provide a great bit of insight into their backstories—like Jason's side stuff with ex-army pal Bret Vogel, or the missions that have Lucia in some all-too-real situations with her mother.

I've played plenty of the game flying solo as both protagonists too, and you'll occasionally get some of this nattering just by hanging around in your abode together. But I can't recommend enough that you find plenty of opportunities to bring them together out in the open world. Even if it's just for 15 minutes here and there, you'll uncover a whole lot about who they were before we first got to know them as the player. And as someone who has really enjoyed learning just about everything about these two as I can, it's been one of my favourite parts of the game so far.

"Apologies if I offended people," says Doug Bowser

Former Nintendo of America president Doug Bowser has posted an apology to the "haters" after sharing some AI slop to celebrate Thanksgiving.

The ex-president shared a post featuring himself at a Thanksgiving table with Bowser and Donkey Kong, with all the telltale signs of AI artwork – namely, it looking terrible – but quickly deleted the post following blowback.

In a post on Twitter, Bowser responds to the reaction, saying, "Apologies if I offended people with my AI generated post. It was sent to me by a friend and it made me smile." He then addresses the "haters," saying "the message remains the same – I wish you a Happy Thanksgiving."

While it could've been an innocent bit of unc posting that you might see from your relatives on Facebook, people have been more annoyed by Bowser's somewhat dismissive attitude towards the responses urging him to not to promote usage of the slop machine and instead work with actual artists.

Others have been expressing disappointment that the former president of a company that values creativity as much as Nintendo would use AI artwork. One response says, "You were the CEO of the American branch of one of the most art focused triple a video game studios," calling the post and response "tone deaf."

Another points out the apology's wording, saying, "Calling people who simply called out the fact that you used ai 'haters' is not the mature look you're going for, Doug."

Bowser took on the role of Nintendo of America president following Reggie Fils-Aimé retiring from the role in 2019. He then led Nintendo through the majority of the Switch era, before stepping down from the role in 2025. Devon Pritchard was named as his successor and currently serves as the president of Nintendo of America.

#3885. After taking seven years to make Persona 6 and four years to make Persona 5, Atlus promises future games will come quicker

"People won't have to wait as long for the next game as they have previously."

Persona 6 is still slowly chugging in the background, but developer Atlus is promising that future games in its beloved RPG series won't take quite as long as they used to.

There was a four year gap between 2012's Persona 4 Golden and the original Persona 5, and it's already been seven years since the expanded Persona 5 Royal first dropped. Despite the sometimes agonising wait filled with countless spin-offs and collaborations with live service games, we've only seen a vague teaser trailer for the next proper Persona.

P-Studio general producer Kazuhisa Wada recently assured folks that the pattern wouldn't repeat again. "Persona 6 is not the end," he said in a Sega Samania interview translated by GamesRadar. "We have been working to make sure that people won't have to wait as long for the next game as they have previously. In order for Persona to grow as an IP, we consider how to live up to people's expectations in terms of creativity and development every day."

Wada doesn't go into any more detail about how Atlus plans to release Persona games quicker. Is the next mainline game already in development alongside Persona 6, or is Atlus just streamlining how it makes games? Either way, the studio seems to have abandoned its divisive habit of returning to and improving its games after a few years - P3 Portable, P4 Golden, P5 Royal. I imagine that'll cut down on wait times, at least somewhat.

"Large-scale RPGs like the Persona series take five years or more to develop," he added. "So there can be a long time between numbered entries."

As for Persona 6 itself, Wada unsurprisingly "can't say much" about the much-hyped, high-schooling, demon-punching game. "But we want our games to demonstrate all of the hard work we've put in. With that in mind, we are creating something better than anything we've made before, and that is hugely satisfying."

We don't know much about Atlus' occult sequel, officially, but a massive information leak earlier in the year revealed a full achievement list for Persona 6 and a bunch of other unreleased games, including Kingdom Hearts 4 and an unannounced Sea of Thieves project. Be wary of online spoilers, then.

#3884. Nightdive's Thief remaster will make the most "infamous" Thief Gold level a little less maddening, by "just kind of pointing the player in the right direction"

On bringing Thieves Guild up to snuff with the Haunted Cathedral and co

1999's Thief Gold is widely considered the definitive incarnation of Thief: The Dark Project, adding three levels to the Looking Glass stealth sim while tidying up some bugs, but it has one grievous failing, in the eyes of many: the notorious Thieves Guild. In this all-new sixth mission, master catburglar Garrett must infiltrate the lair of a gang of pickpockets, after they filch a vase he had his eye on. The lair in question is actually very believable, as a hideout for criminals, in that it resists exploration even with a paper map. It consists of sunken, samey, obtusely arranged rooms that are made all the more headache-inducing by objectives that require a lot of backtracking.

In much the same way that I can admire a finely wrought pair of thumbscrews, I think the Thieves Guild is a clever creation, one that arguably shines when you use every ability or tactic in Garrett's possession rather than trying to ghost it. But it very easily becomes frustrating, to the point that many grizzled housebreakers advise new players to skip the level entirely. The Thieves Guild should be less frustrating in Nightdive's forthcoming Thief: The Dark Project Remastered, thanks to a more revealing spread of environmental textures and various other, furtive adjustments. As with many mods or remasters that speak of boosting the "immersion", I do worry that something valuable is being sacrificed in the process.

In the course of a wide-ranging interview about how they're reworking this most devious of Dark Projects, Nightdive producer Daniel Grayshon explained that the map changes are "more in terms of background tech", than altering the fundamental design or introducing details that oblige different strategies. "They've gone into these levels in a sensible way to fix some practical problems with them, like some issues where you might be able to climb up to a place that you shouldn't have been able to climb up before," he commented.

The Thief remaster team have taken more liberties, seemingly, with some of the Thief Gold maps. "Because some of the levels that were introduced in Thief Gold - they felt quite blocky and quite rushed, maybe, as you go through them," Grayshon explained. "But our team again, they've been able to go through and completely renovate some of these levels. The Opera House now feels in some parts like an actual Opera House, instead of a couple of blocky rooms. So I think players will really look at these and think, oh yeah, these kinds of details make sense, without it being too disruptive or too immersion breaking…"

"One particular - maybe people will consider infamous - level of the Gold package would be the Thieves Guild," Grayshon added. "The Thieves Guild is, if I were to sum it up kind of briefly, it is maybe two hours of walking through what feels like sewers, the same environment over and over again. There was no real visual distinction as to where you are in the level.

"So, we acknowledged pretty quickly that we need to go in and look at the Thieves Guild and fix it up, and what we've been able to do is texture it a lot more effectively. Give areas distinct looks, without compromising any of the gameplay again, like I mentioned. So we've put a bit more signposting around as well. Nothing that's going to be intrusive or immersion breaking again. Just kind of pointing the player in the right direction, as well as some other little things that I'm not going to spoil too much, but I think players will maybe appreciate the effort that we've done for this one."

In general, Nightdive's broad aim has been "bringing those Gold levels up to the quality of the original and then taking all of those levels and then bumping them up to the next level - almost Thief 2 levels of quality in its environment design, especially in some of the mansions, and some of the later levels," Grayshon said. "That's the level we were aiming for."

I have Several Thoughts about Grayshon's thoughts above (yes, people who dislike huffy armchair theory, this is your cue to skip to the comments). One is that I continue to dislike "immersion" as an ideal, though I recognise that many devs just use it as easy shorthand for a bunch of ways of doing art, sound and interface design. I think it often translates to uninvestigated enthusiasm for photorealistic fidelity and experiences that feel "smooth" and "engaging" enough to induce a kind of chemical trance. Many of the games I consider most valuable are cranky and unwilling and jarring, requiring you to think critically about the simulation rather than 'losing yourself' inside it. As regards the original Thief specifically, I enjoy how its nigh-magical stealth induces feelings of wavering dissociation, and keeps me guessing about the solidity of my own body.

Secondly, there's the age-old argument that if you're going to preserve a game faithfully, you should preserve what it did badly. The Thieves Guild is a legend among players, much as Blighttown is among Dark Souls players and the Library is among fans of Halo: Combat Evolved. You learn much about the methodology of Thief at large from the guild's stifling contours, and it's thrilling to witness a bunch of very smart designers take a swing at a concept and not quite connect. I'll try to hold onto that rousing sentiment, when I'm playing the remaster and struggling to remember where they hid that damn vase.

Grand Theft Auto 6 has managed to get its claws into just about everyone. Honestly, I can't go anywhere without hearing something from the soundtrack or someone talking about how much fun it is to joyride around Leonida. And now it's even infested the sports I watch.

To keep non-Formula One fans up to speed, it was the Las Vegas Grand Prix over the weekend, one of the newer circuits on the calendar. Third place went to Oscar Piastri. In second place was his McLaren teammate and previous world champion for 2025, Lando Norris. And first place went to four-time F1 world champion Max Verstappen, not exactly very surprising given his history with the track. But it is a little more impressive when you take into account that Verstappen has also put 40 hours into GTA 6, much of which would have been before the race.

"I played a lot in the evening and in the morning in Vegas," he says in a stream (via IGN), correcting the idea that he actually spent the plane ride home playing GTA 6 instead of spending time doing so around the race. "I mean I can't go out anyways [in the evening and morning], and walk around."

Verstappen did, however, explain that the aspect that GTA 6 has likely affected the most is his ability to play Minecraft, which he had planned to stream later this week: "I'm so bad when I play too many games at the same time. I can't, I just can't."

GTA 6 to Minecraft is certainly a jump, but you can't really blame anyone for trying to maximise their time in Leonida right now. I'll also take any chance to spend every free moment playing the game, the only difference being that instead of subsequently competing in an F1 race and winning it, I spend the next day of work acting like a zombie—a poorly functioning one at that. I suppose people are just built differently, or at least that's what I'll tell myself while I'm on my third cup of coffee in three hours.

#3881. Where to buy a PS5 and PS5 Pro LIVE: Stock is running low this weekend but there are discounts if you know where to look

Keep exploring and earning more as a member.

Get the biggest gaming news, reviews, and releases straight to your inbox.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

In a bizarre blast from the past, PS5 stock is difficult to come by right now. While I thought we were beyond the days of tracking PS5 and PS5 Pro restocks, a surge in demand from Black Friday PS5 deals (not helped by this week's Black Friday GTA 6 deals) has rendered these consoles particularly difficult to find this week.

The problem's not new either. PS5 and PS5 Pro stock has been MIA for a few months in the lead up to Rockstar's blockbuster release. While that Pro model is still absent from the shelves, though, there are ways to buy a PS5 Slim (and even save some cash) in both the US and UK right now.

PS Direct is going to be your first port of call Stateside right now. The retailer has Certified Refurbished consoles readily available on the shelves for $100 off. Meanwhile, the UK is seeing a nearly-£50 saving on a PS5 Digital Edition with GTA 6 and a DualSense included as well.

We're tracking all the latest PS5 and PS5 Pro restocks right here, so if that boosted console even looks at a virtual store shelf you'll know about it below. You'll find the web's current supply of PS5 stock right here, though, with our live updates further down the page.

I was there the first time around, tracking PS5 stock when the console first hit distribution difficulties in 2020 and then reporting on PS5 Pro restocks when the boosted console launched a few years later. Tracking consoles in the big 2026 feels like coming home, then, after years of hunting down hard-to-find gadgets like special edition releases and new Sony and Microsoft hardware.

PS Direct | Certified Refurbished for $100 off

This is my top recommendation for anyone hunting down PS5 stock on the Slim models this weekend. Sony's Certified Refurbished devices come in $100 cheaper than box-fresh consoles, and still pack everything you need in the box and a 12 month warranty. That's a Digital Edition for $499 or a Disc Edition for $549.

GameStop has both the Digital Edition and the Disc versions of the PS5 up for grabs this weekend, with 10% off pre-owned kit to boot. There's nothing here for the Pro model, though.

EE has the best PS5 bundle in the UK right now, with nearly £50 off an extra DualSense and a copy of GTA 6. The full kit would run you £519.99 for the console, £64.99 for the extra controller, and £69.99 for the latest GTA. That's £654.97 in total, while you're paying £605 today.

Going straight to the source will also secure you a PS5 at its regular selling price in the UK, though unlike the US PS Direct doesn't have any refurbished devices up for grabs here. Still, the Slim versions are available, even if the Pro's still MIA.

I wouldn't recommend this bundle over the EE option above, but if stock starts running even lower it's worth keeping as a backup. Amazon has the PS5 Disc console in stock, with an additional DualSense thrown in. However, you'll be waiting until February for shipping on this one.

US friends, I've just had another trawl for PS5 Pro stock and I'm coming up empty handed again. Apologies.

PlayStation Direct, GameStop, Target, Amazon, Best Buy... all absolute crickets. Well all except Walmart, which is trying to charge $1,849.99 for a PS5 Pro. Yeah, no.

I've been covering the PS5 since before it launched (and I was doing this pre-PS4 too if you must know), and the hunger for buying a PS5 feels like when the console first launched. It's pretty mad that we're back in this position. Obviously it's down to a number of factors including the launch of PS5, but there's such a scarcity of machines that it takes me right back to 2020.

Early results on the poll I posted suggest you're all here to buy a PS5 for yourself - the majority upgrading to PS5 Pro (40%) but then 30% of you are desperate to play GTA 6 and the other 30% are getting your first PS5.

There is one PS5 bundle now available at EE and it might appease those of you coming here for a way to play GTA 6 on PlayStation.

For £644.98 at EE, you can get a PS5 Slim Digital with additional DualSense controller, and a £100 EE GameCard to buy GTA 6. It's a really decent bundle as you're getting a saving of around £50 vs buying them separately.

While I continue my rounds, I'd love to know what you're here for so I can help you better!

Guys, I won't lie to you. It's not looking good.

For my UK friends, the EE PS5 GTA 6 bundle is finally out of stock, which was pretty much our last hurrah for the day as we hurtle through to 11pm.

Over the pond in the US, the PlayStation Direct Certified Refurbished Slim console with disc drive is still in stock for $549, but everyone else is outta stock or outta line with their pricings.

Before you go off galavanting across the internet in an attempt to spend your hard-earned cash on a PS5, maybe just think about what you actually need. Trust me I get it, I'm the first one to jump to the best on the market because I want the top of the range, when realistically I don't always need it.

Think about your setup? What are you plugging this PS5 into? Ideally you want a 4K OLED TV with 120Hz, HDMI 2.1, HDR10 and VRR if you're going for the Pro, otherwise you're not really taking full advantage of its features.

What's your budget? Do you really $800/£900 to spend on a console if you want the Pro?

What's most important to you? Value for money? Graphical quality? Performance? Playing physical media?

The Slim Disc edition is probably the best all-rounder, while the Digital is the most cost-effective. The Pro is for those who really do want the best looking games, without worrying too much about enhanced prices. But you think about what you need.

As we continue to search for stock, let alone any deals, it's good to make sure you know what a sensible price is for a PS5 right now, because let's face it, the internet is always eager to rip people off.

First, let's recap the actual current RRPs of the PS5 Slim, PS5 Slim Digital Edition, and PS5 Pro in the US and UK:

These are the prices that Sony upped in April 2026, so definitely bear that in mind when you're looking at deals.

Anything over $50 / £50 more than these prices right now isn't worth the spend, especially as stock is sporadically coming in at RRP or with a game or extra pad bundled for a fair price - not a complete rip off.

Sometimes it's difficult to read between the specs, but it's worth knowing what an investment in a PS5 Pro actually gets you. One of the biggest differences is the fact it comes with a 2TB internal hard drive as standard, vs the relatively measly 825GB of the OG PS5 and the 1TB PS5 Slim.

The graphics and performance are so much better too, thanks to enhanced specs and processing power, and the magic of tech like the PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution, even if it does sound a bit like a superhero (although I guess it kinda is). You will absolutely need a 4K 120Hz or 144Hz TV to make the most of this though, because otherwise it's very much just wasted.

They're the two main differences really, apart from it being a much larger console - which definitely has its pros and cons when it comes to your setup solutions.

With my parting shot for the day, I just want to remind you (if needed) or state outright something you've maybe not had words to articulate: it's OK to just not buy a thing.

You don't need the PS5 Pro! No lives will be saved through your purchase of a video game console, and waiting a little bit longer for an actual deal rather than, say, going into credit card debt is probably the smart move. I don't think being frugal is an ugly thing, especially when we're talking about this amount of money.

It is always, always better to wait for the right deal you feel good about rather than feel like you have to buy something now simply because stock is hard to come by. It'll keep! GTA 6 will still be there, I promise.

I'd hoped that Walmart and Best Buy would get their collective deal together at some point this Black Friday to actually provide meaningful deals on some flavor of PS5, PS5 Slim, or PS5 Pro, but that appears to continue to just be wishful thinking.

A quick look through both seems to indicate they are still flooded with bad, inflated deals with third-party marketplace sellers. In some cases, it would appear to even be the same marketplace vendor. For now, continue to avoid these bad deals, but it's worth keeping tabs on in case something changes.

One aspect of the whole "which version of the PS5 should I get" debate that often seems lacking is that, if you get a version of, say, the PS5 Slim or PS5 Pro that's only digital, you can always pick up a disc drive attachment later. It's not going to solve the problem of finding the exact console you want, but maybe it'll open up addition opens if you're really looking for one with a disc drive only.

PS5 disc drive for Digital Edition consoles | $79 at PS Direct

With another hour gone, what's the status for PS5 and PS5 Pro stock looking like? Well, friend, it's looking... worse than it was.

PS Direct still has the one option going for the refurbished PS5 Slim with disc drive, but GameStop appears to be out of the PS5 Slim and PS5 Pro at the moment with only used and refurbished listings for the regular PS5. UK stock is basically still just that one EE bundle, but it has been holding on since we first caught wind of it earlier. Everywhere else is either wildly inflated or sold out.

Is it worth buying a PS5? Inevitably, this is the question I field most often from folks that don't eat, sleep, and breathe gaming. Makes sense; it's my job, and the expectation is that I would know.

I've said some version of this previously, but basically, if you're asking the question, you probably already have your mind made up. Nobody is dropping a grand or more without being fully committed to the purchase. But if you're truly on the fence, the best answer I've been able to come up with is: if you want to play games that look and play great without investing even more money into a gaming PC, this is your best option.

You can argument about console exclusives and so on until you're blue in the face, but at the end of the day, the PS5 Pro is cheaper than a good PC.

Speaking of inflated resellers, there's not much more than that over at Amazon for the time being when it comes to PS5 consoles, PS5 Pro or otherwise. Similar to other huge retailers, it's a good idea to check back in from time to time, but I'm here to tell you: you don't got to worry about it right now because there's nothing.

Spending all day trying to chase down a PS5 Pro, there's every chance you might at some point wonder, "Should I just hit up, I don't know, eBay or something?" The answer, resoundingly, is no, you absolutely should not.

Even ignoring all of the problems inherent to any site that allows for third-party auctions or resale items, it's simply just... full of bad deals. There's no world I can imagine where it's worth dropping an extra $600 or more just to get your hands on a PS5 Pro right this very moment. The top listing for a 2TB PS5 Pro – with an MSRP, as a reminder, of $899 – over on eBay right now? $1,750. I think not.

In an effort to do my due diligence and check in on likely PS5 Pro retailers, I've hit up most of the big ones several times. Most likely to restock, you know? But just in case you were wondering if some of the less-frequented ones have sneakily added stock, I've got bad news for you: Game, the UK retailer, seemingly... doesn't even have a PS5 (console) listing at the moment, or at least not one I could find.

But who knows? Maybe that'll change. Maybe not.

Speaking of refurbished PS5s: while I'd seen two different versions for sale over at PS Direct earlier, it looks like we're down to just the one refurbished PS5 Slim with disc drive product listing at this point.

Everything else remains as it was, which is to say: we're still out here trying to find you a good deal, but unless you're in the UK and want to take up EE on its bundled offer you might be out of luck for now. And don't fall for the inflated listings at the likes of Walmart and Best Buy.

Sometimes I get asked what the big difference is between refurbished and new and whether refurbished is still worth it when it comes to the PS5 and the short version is: depends on how much you trust PlayStation's recertification process, I guess.

"Every PlayStation certified refurbished product completes a rigorous recertification process that includes full testing that meets the same functional standards as new PlayStation products," PS Direct claims. "Your certified refurbished product works like new."

For me? I don't know. If I'm buying used, or refurbished, I'd hope for a bigger discount.

I find it's a good habit to periodically check back in with trusted retailers from time to time on big consoles like the PS5 Pro. Inevitably, it will drop big tech into the pool when you're least expecting it, and the only way to absolutely miss out is to not be paying attention.

That said, sometimes? Nothing changes. And for now, Best Buy remains completely empty on first-party PS5 Pro options. Bummer.

Rollin here, back at it again! Seems worth trying to answer: why is it so hard to get hold of the PS5 and PS5 Pro in general? The answer is... well, not exactly complicated, but it is multifaceted.

Shortest possible version? All technical hardware has had supply chain issues between parts and tariffs, making them overall more expensive. Then you have the simple fact that the PS5 Pro is, at current, the technical frontrunner for home consoles. You want the best place to play GTA 6 right now? It's on the PS5 Pro.

Add all of this to the usual holiday demand increase, and you get difficult-to-find PS5s, PS5 Slims, and PS5 Pros.

PS Direct's Certified Refurbished PS5 consoles are still firing away on the shelves and GameStop's PS5 Disc Edition is holding firm after the Digital Edition ran out of stock an hour ago.

Amazon, Walmart, and Newegg are still charging well over the odds for a PS5 as well, with no signs of a Pro console in sight.

Meanwhile in the UK, EE is still holding firm with that classic GTA 6 bundle, while PS Direct's supply of Digital Edition consoles is now debatable. My last check keeps turning up errors whenever I try and get on the digital version's page, so it looks like we might be out of luck here.

Amazon UK is estimating a February shipping date for its current PS5 stock, and that's for Prime members. Will it actually take that long, or is the retailer simply over-estimating while its warehouses run out of stock? That's difficult to tell for sure. After all, the store would be expected to receive more stock from Sony itself in that time.

I've seen this kind of movement before, and typically those delivery timings shrink down a little as stock refills warehouses after a period of increased demand. I wouldn't risk it while the PS5 remains available at other retailers, though.

The original PS5 pops back into circulation every now and then, usually via refurbished listings. However, GameStop has pre-owned consoles back in action today - at prices I wouldn't recommend touching. Asking $639.99 for the original device pre-owned when the Slim model is $549 certified refurbished from Sony is pretty ridiculous. Please don't take GameStop up on this offer, things aren't quite that desperate.

Tabs here, back for another hour of PS5 Pro restock hunting while Rollin grabs a bite to eat. I can see GameStop's PS5 Slim stock is starting to wane, so I'll check in there and see if there's any movement. Other than that, let's get a check on the market right now.

That EE GTA 6 bundle appears to still be going strong if you happen to be in the UK. While technically more expensive than just the console, it works out to a deal with the bundle controller and game. And let's be honest here: if you're looking to buy a PS5 Slim or PS5 Pro right now, there's a good chance it's because of GTA 6.

PS5 Digital Edition | GTA 6 | DualSense | £654.97 £605 at EE

That is the question! Ultimately, it is more expensive to get the version of the PS5 (Pro or Slim) with a disc drive. The value add is pretty obvious: either you can or you can't play discs.

As previously noted, there's some argument about whether that's worth the price increase, but to be frank: for me, it's a dealbreaker. We might be on the cusp of an all-digital future, maybe, but for now there's plenty of reasons to keep the ability to play a disc. The price increase is largely negligible if you're already dropping the cash for the console; why not do it right?

When we checked in a couple of hours ago, GameStop had both the PS5 Slim and PS5 Slim Digital Edition at MSRP, but it looks like maybe all good things must end as the digital version is seemingly no longer available. For now, the slightly more expensive version with a disc drive remains available, but who knows for how long.

Friends, I won't lie: PS5 Pro stock status is pretty bleak out there across both the US and UK. What listings there are, that I can find, have been wildly inflated by third-party sellers trying to take advantage of the situation.

GameStop and PS Direct still have some PS5 Slim stock, but PS Direct still appears to be refurbished while GameStop listing is... new, actually. How the turns table! In the UK, the EE bundle we've previously mentioned is still going – but who knows for how long.

While there are technically product listings for various PS5 consoles over at Newegg, they are similarly heavily inflated in the same way that Walmart's prices are inflated. Third-party sellers are the bane of my personal existence, but they're particularly gnarly in this specific scenario.

If you balk at MSRP, don't even think about dipping into these even pricier waters. While PS5s might be hard to come by, they're still being made (for now) and there will be another chance to not get gouged.

There's some question still as to whether the $899 is worth is for the PS5 Pro in 2026. Some on our team argue that there's really nothing in the Pro that makes it so significantly better as to justify the price; it's only worth it to those looking to get the absolute best experience.

I, however, would argue that the value here is that it's the best console on the market in a market that seems to be entirely ditching discs. If that matters to you (and it does to me) and you believe the writing to be on the wall for disc-based consoles then this might be your last, best option for a very long time. Worth getting in now before the price is even higher!

Best Buy previously had PS5 consoles on the shelves with slightly discounted copies of Wolverine. Alongside the rest of Best Buy's PS5 stock, though, they've since sold out. It's worth keeping an eye out here, though, it's been a few days since we've seen Sony's console on these shores.

Very has PS5 Slim consoles in stock and ready to go this morning, but it looks like they've been wiped out. The console was up and available as part of larger bundle deals, but you'll now simply find a PlayStation 5 listing page when you try the same link.

PS5 Pro stock still remains out of reach in both the US and the UK, though one Amazon listing in the former region is giving us reason for hope this morning.

The PS5 Slim is a little easier to find on the shelves - GameStop has both the Disc and Digital versions up for their regular MSRPs while PS Direct still has Certified Refurbished devices at a discount.

Across the pond, the UK is seeing of its better PS5 bundles right now, with EE offering up a PS5 Digital Edition alongside GTA 6 and a spare controller for nearly £50 off.

Walmart allows third party marketplace sellers onto its site, which often wreaks havoc on hard-to-find gadgets. That's happening with both PS5 and PS5 Pro stock this week. You'll find inflated prices in the four figures here right now - but they're not worth sacrificing cash for. Both consoles will be readily available in due time.

Amazon has the PS5 Pro bundled in with a few accessories as separate listings on its store right now. They're all out of stock at the moment, but it looks like there's been activity here recently. Jumping on and off the shelves in smaller releases, the PS5 Pro has been up for grabs here within the last day.

I've seen this from Amazon before. The site sometimes likes to release stock of hard-to-find gadgets in small pockets, frequently throughout the day. Keep that refresh button warm this weekend.

GameStop has both the PS5 Slim and PS5 Slim Digital Edition on the shelves for their regular MSRPs right now, which is a rare treat in itself at the moment. However, you can also grab 10% off a selection of pre-owned accessories at the same time. Separately, the site is also running discounts of up to $40 across PS5 games to boot.

I'm seeing EE's GTA 6 bundle everywhere at the moment, so it's likely moving fast at the retailer. The Digital Edition PS5 is at its regular rate here, with discounts on the game itself and that extra DualSense controller. Considering we're unlikely to see further savings on the console itself this year this is one of the better offers we've seen in some time.

PS5 Digital Edition | GTA 6 | DualSense | £654.97 £605 at EE

There's no need to spend over the odds for PS5 Pro stock if you're coming up short in regular hunts. The console is still difficult to get hold of, but drops have been spotted in the last few days. As an example, this Certified Refurbished device was up for $849 at PS Direct yesterday.

It's been run off the shelves now, but it's still well worth staying optimistic rather than paying reseller fees.

#3880. Nvidia reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO following alleged affairs, as US government support renders 'please give me my job back, go USA' a highly persuasive plea

Sexy leather jacket man's successor is exact same sexy leather jacket man, it turns out

Yep, he's back. Less than two weeks after Jensen Huang resigned from being CEO of Nvidia following reports of multiple affairs, the company's board have reinstated him "effective immediately".

"The board of directors voted unanimously to reinstate Mr Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr Huang, after which the board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candour and ability to lead Nvidia," the company announced. "In the process of reaching its decision, the board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk."

"The board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," added recently appointed chairman Harvey Jones, who'll remain in the post following Huang's return. Colette Kress, who served as interim CEO during Huang's short break, will go back to just being chief financial officer.

"I am honoured to return to Nvidia and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution," Huang declared. "I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment."

Oh, and Nvidia's board added that the independent investigation they set in motion "in light of recent reporting that Mr. Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort" will "proceed to conclusion". Huang "fully supports the investigation and is committed to cooperating with it", they noted.

Since resigning amid the scandal, Huang had made it clear he'd be open to returning to his post if the Nvidia board okayed it and had several powerful people either call for his reinstatement or declare they'd consider hiring him. "The country needs Jensen’s leadership at Nvidia in order to ensure the success and prosperity of not only the company, but the American economy," one such advocate, US president Donald Trump, has reportedly posted to cursed hellcape Truth social. Huang is a "great patriot and national treasure", the Trumpeter added.

So, there you go. I'm not saying that you're totally immune to consequences for alleged actions that'd lose any normal person their job for far more than 11 days if you're mates with the American president, but it sure does look like that, doesn't it? Hope Nvidia didn't throw out any leather jackets Huang couldn't manage to carry out of the building with him.

#3879. GTA 6 is officially the biggest entertainment launch of all time, selling 32.5 million pre-sale copies and a bonkers $3.79 billion in its first day

"We are incredibly humbled by the response."

Surprise, surprise - GTA 6 is officially the biggest entertainment launch of all time, surpassing its predecessor's 13-year-long record and the already optimistic analyst estimates.

Rockstar Games today confirmed that its cultural juggernaut sold a staggering 32.5 million pre-release copies across PS5 and Xbox Series X/S before its official worldwide launch on the 19th of November. By the end of its first day on sale, GTA 6 managed to rake in a frankly absurd $3.79bn. Not a bad haul.

As Rockstar was quick to brag, the whopping performance means GTA 6 set "a new record for entertainment across any medium" by "becoming the biggest entertainment launch in history."

For context, GTA 5 made around $800m in its opening 24 hours more than a decade ago. That mammoth debut almost looks quaint next to GTA 6's stunning numbers, although it's notable GTA 5 didn't launch immediately in Japan or Brazil - GTA 6 is available in almost every market with access to PlayStation and Xbox consoles.

"It is with immense gratitude that we enter a new chapter of Rockstar Games with the release of Grand Theft Auto VI," said Rockstar co-founder and company president, Sam Houser, in a recent press release. "We are incredibly humbled by the response from players around the world and we couldn't be more excited to share this moment with you."

Previous estimates guessed that GTA 6 had sold almost 25m copies ($2.5bn in revenue) on day one. It's fair to say the game's staggering performance blew even those sky-high projections out of the water.

Every early indicator pointed to GTA 6's inevitably record-breaking launch. Parent company Take-Two previously said the game was tracking "well above expectations," as the crime fest sold more pre-orders than any other game in PlayStation Store and Xbox Store history.

The only question now is whether GTA 6 can ever outsell GTA 5's mammoth 230m copies, which it reached thanks to a very healthy cadence of GTA Online updates. How high GTA 6 can go will likely depend on its multiplayer offering, though Rockstar hasn't said anything concrete about that just yet.

"A game of opposites and awe, minute detail and impossible scale, Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again with GTA 6. An irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action - and a load more after that," Chris Tapsell gushed in Eurogamer's GTA 6 review.

Stealing an ATM in GTA 6 requires a few different things: a winched vehicle to haul it out of the wall and drive off, plus the dye pack jammer that stops marked bills from exploding pink all over your lovely cash.

There are two ways to get a winched truck. The video above shows a location at the crop duster landing strip in Frogswater where you can steal one, but you can also mod any truck at a mod shop to add a winch.

If you don't have a truck to mod, there's a unique one you can steal from the Kolt & Associates June Warehouse robbery in Port Gellhorn, just south of Sarena's Bargain Store, which you could then register with Moses and mod at Wasteland Off-Road in the north of the town. You can also get a winched truck around the back of Yasmani's vape shop in Little Cuba—the fence who gives you the ATM tip offs.

You'll also need the dye pack jammer, which you get in the Chapter 3 main mission, Credit Check, for Raul. Once you have both of these, you're ready to rob an ATM. If you complete all three of Yasmani's jewelry thefts (also in Chapter 3), he'll call a little later and offer tips about full ATMs, giving you three for free that you have a 24 hour window to hit. Here's how to steal them

For Yasmani's tipped-off ATMs I got about 11k-ish per time, so not terrible, but likely not the best way to make money unless you get really efficient at it and invest in a proper getaway winch truck.

#3877. GTA 6 features the series' first non-binary character, says actor Jesse James Rose, and players can't hurt them

Grand Theft Auto 6 features the first non-binary character in the series' history, according to actor Jesse James Rose, who plays the role of a museum curator in the game.

"I can FINALLY share that I play the first-ever nonbinary character in the Grand Theft Auto franchise!" Rose wrote on Instagram.

"Absolutely wild to find out THIS was the super-secret game I spent weeks and 17 NDAs filming 3 years ago."

"I shot this back in my they/them days, and everyone on production ensured I was comfortable and gendered correctly," Rose wrote. The project was kept so secret that Rose wasn't told what it was during filming and only recently learned it was GTA 6.

"GTA was one of the most inclusive & caring sets I've ever been on," they added.

A post shared by Jesse James Rose ✨ (@jamesissmiling)

The role was shot entirely through motion capture, which meant wearing "a unitard made of dots every day". Rose also says steps were taken to protect the character in-game: "To mitigate anti-trans violence, I was assured that players would not be able to inflict violence against my character."

A whole day of the shoot was spent scanning Rose's face, including hours of pulling different expressions. At one point Rose couldn't move a particular muscle, and worried the scan had been ruined, but the director was thrilled.

"That right there is exactly why we'll never use AI," he said, according to Rose. "A computer could never come up with the face you just made."

"Remember, in a world consumed with Generative AI, the largest video game in history chose human labour to preserve the integrity of the game," Rose added.

Rose did raise some concerns about pay, though.

"Despite being paid well for my time on set, I'll never see a residual check for my work," Rose wrote, explaining that this is part of SAG’s contract with game developers. As a union leader at one of SAG's sister unions, Rose said there's still "a long way to go to ensure arts workers are fairly compensated for our labour".

Rose also says many other trans people worked on GTA 6, both in front of the camera and behind it. "SO many trans people besides me are featured in GTA VI as other roles, designers, writers, etc... take a note, theatre and TV! We are employable & profitable!!!"

Finally, Rose voiced support for Rockstar's UK staff. "UK-based workers at Rockstar Games are currently voting on whether to unionise, and I sincerely hope their efforts are successful," Rose wrote. "Every arts worker should have a stable job with benefits and fair working conditions protected by a union."

GTA 6 is out now on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. It launched on Thursday, although some have been getting in on the action earlier, as a whopping 2m Xbox players in the UK and US took advantage of the trick of changing their console's country. Even New Zealand's tourist board tipped a wink to the sudden influx of virtual 'visitors', telling them "We'd love to have you". It also cheekily offered a video of cheerful tourists admiring the country's resplendent natural beauty. "Life," read the accompanying caption, "because we're getting GTA 6 first."

If you're hoping to make cool miniatures, props, and all manner of nerdy goodies, Black Friday 3D printer deals provide so many great offers for beginners. Actually, it's hands down the best time to dive in; both machines and materials typically hit record lows, so you're unlikely to get a better (or cheaper) opportunity.

Because you aren't short on options, I've rounded up a couple of my favorite newcomer-friendly machines and the gear you'll need to kick things off. These have all been slashed in price for 2026's Black Friday 3D printer deals, so beginners can get into the hobby for as little as possible. These have all been chosen based on my years of experience testing 3D printers at GamesRadar+ as well as reporting on the sale, so rest assured you're getting maximum value for money here.

If you're not sure what to go for, don't worry; here's a quick breakdown. Want to make terrain, props, tokens, or generally useful stuff like storage boxes or dividers for the best board games? Filament printers are the way to go. Looking for incredibly high-detail miniatures or more detailed cosplay gear? Resin printers are what you want. I've included my entry-level picks for both that come from extensive hands-on experience, and they're what I use at home right now.

No matter whether you're new to 3D printing or have experience with the hobby, I think this may be my favorite filament machine. Besides being incredibly easy to use (something I praised in my Elegoo Centauri Carbon 2 Combo review), it comes with multi-color print functionality so that you can create more advanced projects without having to manually swap out material. Plus, it being so enclosed keeps things tidy and much quieter too. To cap things off, I'm pretty sure that's a record low price.UK: £398 £329 at Elegoo (with code)

Even though they're smaller spools (most normal ones are 1KG, whereas these are 250g each), this multi-color pack is a great way to kick off your hobby and provide the widest range of shades as cheaply as possible. It's never been cheaper than it is now for this year's Black Friday 3D printer deals.UK: £34.99 £28.25 at Amazon

If you want a fuss-free, foolproof way of printing resin miniatures that isn't going to make you want to tear your hair out, this is the perfect choice. As noted in my Anycubic Photon P1 review, it's able to overcome any problem you throw at it due to a user-friendly interface, a heated vat to avoid failures if you're printing in a colder environment, incredibly high print resolutions, and a new 'Wave Release Technology' for a better overall print. When you throw in good positioning accuracy and stability to avoid failures, it's a great choice.UK: £649 £399 at Anycubic

If you're buying a resin 3D printer, you'll need one of these - a wash and cure machine. That's because models aren't ready once they're made in the printer; they've got to be rinsed off with either IPA or water (depending on the resin you've used) and then cured using UV lamps. It's not a particularly drawn-out process, but it is important. If you're getting Anycubic's machine, I'd go for its accompanying Wash and Cure system for ease.UK: £113 £79 at Anycubic

Want the easiest entry-point to resin 3D printing with the least fuss? I'd recommend water-washable resin, because you don't then need to worry about grabbing smelly IPA as well. With this material, you can just use normal water in your wash and cure machine which is much, much easier to then dispose of.UK: £21.80 £13.59 at Amazon

#3874. GTA 6 has a 99 Metascore from critics, but players are review bombing it

Grand Theft Auto 6 might be one of the best-reviewed games of all time, but you wouldn't know it from its Metacritic user score.

While critics have given Rockstar's latest a Metascore of 99, its user score has dropped to 5.6 out of 10 at the time of writing, which Metacritic classifies as "mixed or average". Of the 54,000+ ratings left, 44 percent are "negative".

The score had previously dropped into the red, but has since recovered a little.

Some negative reviews raise genuine complaints, such as the game's 30FPS cap on console, while others take issue with how much of the story focuses on Jason and Lucia's relationship instead of the crime-spree antics of past games.

"Expectations might've killed this game," states one 0/10 review. "The hype that something otherworldly would come to be flopped. The hyperrealism makes it feel slow, mundane and boring. Its a tecnichal [sic] advancement for sure but for the wrong reasons. Goodlooks zero personality type stuff. Its not as edgy as the rest of the gta games. And thats exactly my problem like is not funny. The game gets carried by its visuals and radio stations. Certain limitations make it feel like not gta and new features make it feel like not gta. In the end it feels like a life simulator and the point of gaming is to escape from reality."

"Genuinely hated almost every minute of this experience," wrote another. "After years of waiting and an absurd amount of hype, GTA VI somehow managed to leave me more frustrated than entertained. The excessive sexual content gets exhausting, and instead of adding anything meaningful to the experience, it often feels like Rockstar is desperately trying to shock its audience.

"The story is painfully disappointing, the writing fails to keep me invested, and I honestly couldn't care less about what happens to most of these **** gameplay isn't doing the game any favours either. Glitches, bugs, annoying inconsistencies, and frustrating moments constantly get in the way of actually enjoying the experience. It's ridiculous that a game of this scale, backed by a studio with Rockstar's resources, can feel this rough. I expected a polished experience, not a glorified debugging ****."

Others point to "woke" and "DEI" agendas.

"A major step down in the writing department compared to previous instalments coupled with the obvious DEI-fication, unfun realism and the resulting player freedom restrictions leave a sour taste in the otherwise detailed gorgeous open world," said one reviewer. Another unhappy player wrote: "Shameful DEI hijacked cuck simulator, the most overrated game of all time and it's not even close."

#3872. GTA 6 is crashing on some PS5s with error CE-108255-1 - here's what you can try

Some Grand Theft Auto 6 players on PS5 say the game keeps crashing with error code CE-108255-1, and in some cases, it's stopping them from progressing through the story.

"The game runs perfectly fine for a while. I can complete missions and chapters without any issues, but then it suddenly crashes after around 40 minutes and sends me back to the PS5 home screen", wrote one Reddit user. They added that other games, including GTA 5 and For Honor, run without crashing.

Another player told Dexerto that GTA 6 worked fine until Pipework, an early mission that introduces Mandy, but now crashes "every time I use the plunger or stand around the sink with it", which means they can’t progress.

Some PS5 Pro owners say the game crashes during the opening prologue, either at the same point every time or a few seconds in, and they haven't been able to play since launch.

Others say they've tried the usual fixes, such as clearing their console's cache, rebuilding the database, factory resetting their PS5, and even downloading the game three times, but nothing has worked thus far.

It's not just PS5 players that are struggling, either; some Xbox Series X players have reported crashes too, with one saying the game sometimes crashes after just 15 minutes.

Rockstar hasn't yet acknowledged the crashes or said whether a patch is on the way, and its own support is sending players with console errors to PlayStation or Xbox directly for help.

Unfortunately, there's no firm fix just yet. PlayStation's support page describes CE-108255-1 simply as "an error occurred with the game/application”, and its only advice is to "try updating your game". Highlight GTA 6 on your home screen, press Options, and choose Check for Update.

#3871. Finally, some former Valorant and Sky devs have answered the call for a Peak-style platformer about throwing a cat through a hole in spacetime

It's embarrassing that we had to wait this long

As a mature and sophisticated artform, videogames offer answers to many of life's important questions, such as "how many spaceships is too many spaceships?" (a trick question, obviously) or "which 12th century BC civilisation was better at playing Age of Empires 2?" Lately, I have been wrestling with the enigma of how I should transport a sleeping cat in a snowglobe up a psychedelic mountain. According to Whisk, I should phone a friend.

In this first-person co-op platformer - created in Unreal Engine, with both online multiplayer and splitscreen support - you and a mate play Luna and Foam, two rock-hopping magic children with nothing better to do than lob hermetically sealed felines through tears in reality itself. Egad! Apparently the cats are fine with this. You'll have to work together to traverse astral watercolour landscapes, hurling and catching the kitty while trying not to tumble into the abyss.

You can also catch each other's arms and haul each other onto safe ground, which puts this in approximately the same bracket as the well-liked Peak. Other Neat Tricks include bouncing the starry-eyed moggies from soap bubbles, swinging from strands of green snot (?), and springboarding from tornadoes.

The cats remain blissfully unconscious throughout, smiling in their slumber right up to the point when you crack their crystal prisons. If you're familiar with cats, the penalty for breaking their domes may seem rather mild. I was hoping for something along the lines of Peter Puppy having a rage-out in Earthworm Jim.

Would it surprise you to learn that one or more of the people working on Whisk is a former developer of Sky: Children of Light, the open world swoop 'em up from thatgamecompany? I imagine you might not consider that startling – the two games both look a little like the result of somebody inhaling burnt banana skins. But you might be giddier to hear that one or more of the Whisk devs is also a veteran of Riot's Counter-Strike descendant Valorant. I'm pretty sure Valorant doesn't have any cat-throwing, but I'm prepared to be proven wrong.

It's coming to Steam early access early in 2027, and there's a demo on Steam right now with eight levels and 10 cats to "rescue". People are already bragging in the forums about their leaderboard placements – monsters!

May I remind you, GTA 6 wasn't the only game to come out in the last two weeks. Clicky Islands, a fun throwback island builder published by Palworld company Pocketpair, arrived earlier in the month, and according to the publisher's estimates, it's doing very well indeed.

On Twitter, John 'Bucky' Buckley, the head of publishing and communications at Pocketpair, takes a second to highlight just how successful the game's been. "Clicky Islands launched ten days ago, and it's smashed every target!" he writes. "Really proud to be supporting this game and the two Polish wizards who cooked it up!"

It is a delightful little gem that merges citybuilding and idle game ideas. Essentially, you land on a remote island, and start making it more habitable for your people, but how you do that is distinctly streamlined – you mostly just click around and let things be built, gradually accruing more resources.

Clicky Islands launched 10 days ago, and it's smashed every target! Really proud to be supporting this game and the two Polish wizards who cooked it up! 🇵🇱 A devilishly addictive incremental game that blends clicker elements with city building! A real gem! https://t.co/oOu58lP7IrNovember 26, 2026

As Pocketpair's monster-collecting survival adventure continues to grow, more opportunities for games like this can and will emerge, and it's good to see that money and energy being put to good use. If Clicky Islands is anything to go by, I'd keep an eye on what else the publisher may have in store.

Meanwhile, Buckley's been teasing that we'll hear more about Palfarm and the coveted Palworld 1.1 soon. No rest for the wicked – unless Rockstar's about to put something out, that is.
